title: Sex representation and sex-specific treatment effects in randomized trials of novel cardio-renoprotective therapies for chronic kidney disease
author: Ioannis Bellos

steps.title: Define Study Eligibility Criteria
steps.instruction: Identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that meet specific population and intervention requirements.

substeps.instruction: Include adult patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD); exclude trials where CKD patients are a subgroup unless CKD-specific results are reported separately.
Include interventions from the following classes: SGLT2 inhibitors, GLP-1 receptor agonists, and ns-MRAs, evaluated against placebo or any active intervention.
Ensure trials report the number or proportion of female participants or provide sufficient data to derive this information.
Exclude observational studies, post-hoc analyses, secondary analyses of previously published trials, case series, and non-randomized studies.

steps.title: Conduct Systematic Literature Search
steps.instruction: Perform a comprehensive search for eligible trials across electronic databases.

substeps.instruction: Search PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials from inception to the final search date.
Combine controlled vocabulary terms and free-text keywords related to CKD and the specified drug classes.
Perform literature search and study selection independently using two reviewers.
Resolve discrepancies through discussion and consensus, involving a third reviewer if necessary.

steps.title: Extract Study and Participant Data
steps.instruction: Use a standardized data extraction form to collect study-level, authorship, and participant characteristics independently via two reviewers.

substeps.instruction: Extract study-level data: year of publication, trial name/registry identifier (e.g., NCT number), geographical region, population characteristics, intervention and comparator, trial phase, blinding status, funding source, presence of run-in phase, sex-stratified randomization, requirements for background renin–angiotensin system inhibitor therapy, requirements for prior cardiovascular disease, albuminuria and eGFR inclusion criteria, BMI inclusion criteria, requirements for pregnancy testing/contraception/exclusion of women of childbearing potential, placebo or active treatment comparator, total sample size, primary outcome, and reporting of major clinical outcomes (cardiovascular and kidney).
Extract authorship data: sex and specialty of the first author, sex and specialty of the last author, and total number of female authors.

Extract baseline participant characteristics (when available): proportion of White race, prevalence of diabetes mellitus, prevalence of cardiovascular disease, median or mean age, BMI, eGFR, urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), and duration of follow-up.

steps.title: Analyze Female Representation
steps.instruction: Assess female representation using the Enrollment Disparity Difference (EDD) approach.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the observed proportion of female participants (Pobs) as the number of women divided by the total sample size.

Derive the expected proportion of women (Pexp) from Global Burden of Disease Study sex-specific prevalence estimates of CKD, using separate estimates for diabetic kidney disease and non-diabetic CKD based on the trial population.
Calculate EDD using the formula: EDD = Pobs - Pexp.
Estimate the standard error (SE) of the EDD using the formula: SE(EDD) = sqrt[Pobs (1-Pexp) / N], where N is the total number of participants.
Pool trial-specific EDD estimates using random-effects meta-analysis and report results as pooled EDD values with 95% confidence intervals.
Assess between-study heterogeneity using the I² statistic.
Perform random-effects meta-regression to identify trial characteristics associated with disparities in female enrollment.

steps.title: Analyze Sex-Specific Treatment Effects
steps.instruction: Evaluate treatment effects for hard outcomes (composite cardiovascular and composite kidney outcomes).

substeps.instruction: Extract sex-specific effect estimates (e.g., hazard ratios) and standard errors for each trial.
Perform a random-effects meta-regression using sex as a moderator, weighted by the inverse variance of the trial-specific estimates.
Determine if a significant sex–treatment interaction exists based on the p value for the sex covariate (p < 0.05).
